title: Colby vs Williams: tuition, size, location
summary: Colby College (Colby) versus Williams College (Williams). Also searched as Williams vs Colby. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Colby College and Williams College are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. Colby College, located in Waterville, has an undergraduate enrollment of 2,407 students, while Williams College in Williamstown enrolls 2,076 undergraduates. Tuition costs are similar, with Colby charging $69,600 and Williams $68,560 for in-state students. These differences in enrollment size, location, and tuition reflect distinct characteristics between the two colleges.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Colby College and Williams College have comparable tuition costs for both in-state and out-of-state students, with Colby charging $69,600 and Williams $68,560. Despite the similarity in tuition, there is a notable difference in the median debt of students who complete their degrees. Graduates from Colby College carry a median debt of $19,157, whereas those from Williams College have a lower median debt of $12,761. These financial figures highlight distinctions in the cost burden experienced by students at each institution.

When comparing Colby vs Williams, the tuition fees are nearly identical, but the median debt upon graduation differs significantly. This suggests variations in financial aid, borrowing patterns, or other economic factors affecting students at the two colleges. Understanding these cost elements is important for prospective students evaluating their potential financial commitments.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Colby College and Williams College both offer undergraduate education in distinct New England settings. Colby College is situated in Waterville, Maine, and enrolls approximately 2,407 undergraduate students. In contrast, Williams College is located in Williamstown, Massachusetts, with a slightly smaller undergraduate population of about 2,076 students. Both institutions emphasize a liberal arts education, but their campus environments reflect their different geographic and community contexts.

When comparing Colby vs Williams, the differences in enrollment size and location contribute to unique campus experiences. Colby's larger student body in a Maine city contrasts with Williams' smaller college town setting in Massachusetts, influencing aspects such as campus culture, student engagement, and local resources available to students.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Colby College and Williams College are both accredited institutions, ensuring that they meet established standards of quality in higher education. Accreditation is a critical factor for colleges as it validates the academic programs and institutional operations. While specific accrediting bodies are not detailed here, both colleges maintain recognized accreditation status, which supports their eligibility for federal funding and the transferability of credits. When comparing Colby vs Williams, accreditation serves as a foundational similarity that underscores their commitment to academic excellence and institutional integrity.

sections.heading: Pick Colby if
paragraphs: Pick Colby if you are seeking admission to a highly selective private nonprofit college with an admission rate of approximately 7.1%. These factors indicate a rigorous academic environment with a high level of student success.
